The resampled images match those references, but compression settings may differ. All my other GTA V scratch files are deleted.. Judge: I picked pair 1 B, pair 2 A, pair 3 A and pair 4 A. The other four frames share one look (Singapore streets, shophouses, rain trees, a red sports car, and a gameplay HUD in two of them), and they lose for the same reasons. (1) Ground near the camera is clean and uniform: asphalt, tiles and kerbs have no visible grain, no wear and weak contact shadows, with leaf decals scattered on top. (2) The low sun does not reach the foreground: no long shadows toward the camera, no grazing sheen on the road, no backlit glow in foliage, and little haze with distance. Their skies are bright painted domes with cartoon clouds. (3) Background skylines look like placeholder boxes, and car models repeat. (4) The player character is far less detailed than the environment. Their strengths are dense, on-theme set dressing (scooters, planters, bike racks, signage, Peranakan tiles) and soft modern lighting, which is why pair 3 was close. The winners are more deliberately composed and lit, and their surfaces show age (rust, grime, peeling paint, rutted dirt). Fixing the near field and making it respond to the sun would close most of the gap. Caveats: the test was not truly blind. Three of the winning frames carry a visible Grand Theft Auto V watermark, and the HUD marks two of the others as gameplay captures. The winners are also curated press shots compared against raw gameplay frames. I judged only what each frame shows, and the gaps I name are in the rendered content, not the framing. Only two frames truly impressed me: pair 1 B and pair 4 A.
